guide.title: Chaplin, Connecticut: A Deacon's Bequest and a Bypassed Village
guide.intro: Chaplin was incorporated in May 1822 from parts of Hampton, Mansfield and Windham, named for Deacon Benjamin Chaplin, an early landowner and surveyor whose bequest created the town. Chaplin left three hundred pounds in his will to build a meetinghouse; the church went up between 1812 and 1815 on Chaplin Hill, and residents incorporated the town in his honor. Between 1820 and 1850, roughly 25 homes, a tavern and several stores were built along the curved road by the river near the church — the village standing today. When Route 198 was straightened in 1929, the new road bypassed the old village, leaving Chaplin Street intact; it received local Historic District designation in 1974 and was listed on the National Register in 1978, having survived because it lacked industrial water power and was bypassed by the railroads. The Witter House on Chaplin Street, built 1820-1821, housed three generations of physicians named Oren Witter.

sections.heading: A deacon's bequest
sections.body: Chaplin was incorporated in May 1822 from parts of Hampton, Mansfield and Windham, named for Deacon Benjamin Chaplin, an early landowner and surveyor. Chaplin left three hundred pounds in his will to build a meetinghouse; the church went up between 1812 and 1815 on Chaplin Hill, and residents incorporated the town in his honor. Between 1820 and 1850, roughly 25 homes, a tavern, a general store, a dry goods store and a merchant's store were built along the curved road paralleling the Natchaug River near the church. Silk manufacturing and other small industries grew along the river, which bisects the town diagonally from northwest to southeast. When Route 198 was straightened in 1929, the new road bypassed the old village, leaving Chaplin Street intact; it received local Historic District designation in 1974 and was listed on the National Register in 1978. The Witter House, built 1820-1821, was home to three generations of physicians named Oren Witter, the first of whom served as Chaplin's first town clerk.

sections.heading: Getting there
sections.body: Chaplin is a car-only destination: US Route 6 runs straight through town on the way from Willimantic/Windham toward Hampton and Brooklyn, and CT Route 198 begins at that US 6 junction and heads north across the Natchaug River toward Eastford and US 44. Interstate 395 is reached by following US 6 east toward Killingly, where it becomes an expressway near the interstate. There is no passenger rail station in Chaplin or anywhere in Windham County; the nearest trains are the CTrail Hartford Line and Amtrak on the New Haven-Hartford-Springfield corridor well to the west. The only railroad that once crossed Chaplin is now the Air Line State Park Trail.

faq.question: How do I get to Chaplin?
faq.answer: By car — US Route 6 runs straight through town, and CT Route 198 begins there and heads north to Eastford. There is no passenger rail station in Chaplin or anywhere in Windham County.

faq.question: Is there a train to Chaplin?
faq.answer: No. The railroad that once crossed Chaplin is now the Air Line State Park Trail. The nearest CTrail Hartford Line and Amtrak service runs on the New Haven-Hartford-Springfield corridor, well to the west.

faq.question: What is Diana's Pool?
faq.answer: A rock-walled pool on the Natchaug River, Chaplin's best-known natural landmark and a popular local swimming spot. It is unstaffed with no dedicated parking or facilities, and this stretch of river includes Class IV rapids — use caution.

faq.question: What is the Chaplin Historic District?
faq.answer: A 40-acre district along Chaplin Street, centered on the 1812-1815 Congregational Church, with Federal and Greek Revival houses that survived unaltered because the village lacked industrial water power and was bypassed by the railroads and by the 1929 realignment of Route 198.

faq.question: Is there a hotel in Chaplin?
faq.answer: No hotel, inn, motel or B&B could be verified inside Chaplin. The nearest options are The Inn on Storrs in Mansfield Center and The Inn at Woodstock Hill in Woodstock, though the latter's restaurant is open for private events only.

places.name: Chaplin Historic District
places.address: Chaplin Street (off CT Route 198), Chaplin, CT 06235
places.summary: A 40-acre district running about 0.8 miles along Chaplin Street, centered on the 1812-1815 Congregational Church, with the former town hall (1840), the Ross Memorial Library (1911) and Eaton's Store (1850) among the landmarks. Listed on the National Register in 1978; a public streetscape viewable from Chaplin Street at any time.

places.name: Air Line State Park Trail (Chaplin section)
places.address: Trail parking at Chewink Road and Lynch Road, Chaplin, CT 06235
places.summary: The Air Line State Park Trail runs roughly 50 miles across eastern Connecticut from Thompson to Portland on a rail bed built in the 1870s, passing through Chaplin. Open to walkers, hikers, bikers and horseback riders, with cross-country skiing and snowshoeing in winter; free, leashed pets allowed.

places.name: Natchaug State Forest
places.address: Off CT Route 198 north of Chaplin village
places.summary: Established in 1917, Natchaug State Forest covers 13,438 acres across six towns including Chaplin, Ashford and Eastford. DEEP describes it as popular for horse trails, fishing and riverfront picnic sites; it holds the site of the birthplace of Union General Nathaniel Lyon.

places.name: Chaplin Public Library
places.summary: Housed in a 1940s elementary school renovated and rededicated in 2000, just off Route 198 next to the Chaplin Senior Center. Open Monday and Wednesday 10 a.m.-6 p.m., Friday 2-6 p.m., Saturday 10 a.m.-1 p.m.

places.name: Edward Garrison Park
places.address: c/o Chaplin Town Hall, 495 Phoenixville Road, Chaplin, CT 06235
places.summary: Chaplin's principal public park, open to the general public sunrise to sunset daily; no open fires, dogs must be leashed and cleaned up after. Has hosted community concerts.

places.name: Baker's Dozen of Chaplin
places.summary: A counter-service coffee-and-baked-goods shop inside a convenience store, one of ten Baker's Dozen shops clustered in Connecticut's Quiet Corner and southeastern shoreline. Open weekdays 5 a.m.-7 p.m., Saturday-Sunday 5:30 a.m.-7 p.m.

places.name: Dunkin' (Chaplin)
places.summary: The only nationally branded coffee stop in town, attached to Zlotnick's gas station on US Route 6. Call ahead to confirm hours.
